Contributing to tflspec

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Issues and pull requests are welcome at https://github.com/ichirio/tflspec. For anything non-trivial, open an issue first so we agree on the approach. A good first contribution is a template: see dev/adding-a-template.md.

Workflow

  1. Fork the repository and clone your fork.
  2. Add the original repository as upstream: git remote add upstream https://github.com/ichirio/tflspec.git.
  3. Start from the current main: git fetch upstream, then git checkout -b <your-branch> upstream/main.
  4. Make the change, commit, and push the branch to your fork.
  5. Open a pull request against main of ichirio/tflspec.

Branch from main and open the pull request against main. (The maintainers work from next; yours does not.) The maintainers add labels and merge. If your branch falls behind, rebase it on upstream/main: the section “Rebase a topic branch on upstream/main” in AGENTS.md has the steps. Keep your fork’s main up to date the same way (“Update the fork’s main” there).

Rules

  • Do not change Version: in DESCRIPTION, NEWS.md or the version line of the AI manuals. The maintainers set the version.
  • One change per pull request. Do not stack pull requests.
  • When sheet columns, template arguments or the generated code change, tflplanner may need a follow-up (a new column needs a translation there). Say so in the pull request; the maintainers run tflplanner’s tests.
  • Use fictional data only: Example Pharma and the bundled sample studies (adsl, adae, adlb …). Never put a company’s specifications or data in code, tests, issues or pull requests.
  • R source is ASCII-only. Write other characters as \uXXXX escapes. Non-ASCII is fine in comments and roxygen.
  • Change the code, its tests and its roxygen text together.
  • Keep the line endings of the files you edit.
  • Explain a feature by what it does, not by comparison with another package; name another package only when it is the actual subject (an engine, a dependency, an adapter).

The change record

Record the change in the PR description. A PR never edits NEWS.md, CHANGELOG.md or Version:, and there is no separate memo file. Fill the template’s User-visible change (for NEWS) field without being asked: one or two bullets in NEWS style (what a user can now do, or what is fixed, named by its function or argument), or “none” for an internal change; then “Breaking: no”, or “Breaking: yes” with the migration. The maintainers write NEWS.md from the merged PRs at release. For example:

## User-visible change (for NEWS)

- `tfl_tpl()`'s `ae_pt_freq` takes `min_pct`: a preferred term with less than
  that percent of subjects in every arm is left out (`min_pct_in` says where
  the percent must be met).

Breaking: no

Checks before a push

Install the package from your branch, then run the tests of the area you changed. <area> is part of a test file’s name: ae-pt-freq runs tests/testthat/test-tpl-ae-pt-freq.R. A name’s underscores become hyphens there.

install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")   # or devtools::install()
Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN = "true")                           # run the tests CRAN would skip
testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat", filter = "<area>",
                   package = "tflspec", load_package = "installed")

package and load_package run the tests against the installed package. Without them, the tests of the help pages (tpl-docs, tpl-help) fail with could not find function ".tpl_rd".

Run the lint check, and devtools::document() after any roxygen change. Commit the man/*.Rd files it changes for your work, and revert the ones it changes for nothing you touched.

lintr::lint_package()      # should be clean
devtools::document()

A pull request against main runs the full R-CMD-check: R CMD check on ubuntu (R devel, release, oldrel and 4.2), macOS and Windows, with ggplot2 3.5 and 4.0 and the oldest cards and cardx. It also builds the pkgdown site. A lint job runs on every pull request; run lintr::lint_package() before a push too, so that it does not fail there. (The maintainers’ pull requests into next run the lint job and a quick test job.)
